title: Split Tender with Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards: Order of Application and Allocation to Purchase Records
content:
### Standard

1. Several Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards can pay one transaction, up to each card kind's limit on cards of that kind per transaction.
2. Finch Notes are applied before any card. The cards are then applied in this order: first the Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card; then cards that carry an expiry date, the earliest expiry date first; then every other card, the lowest balance first.
3. Each card pays at most its balance, and only toward merchandise outside that card kind's excluded purchases.
4. A card's redemption is recorded against each purchase record it pays. The card's amount is allocated among those purchase records in proportion to the records' amounts due; each record's share is rounded half up to the cent, and any remainder is placed on the highest-priced record.

### Order of application

| Position | Tender | Ordering within the position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Finch Notes | Before any card |
| 2 | Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card | — |
| 3 | Cards with an expiry date | Earliest expiry date first |
| 4 | Every other card | Lowest balance first |

### Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

*Example A — order.* A hypothetical in-store transaction has $120.00 of merchandise, all of it outside every presented card's excluded purchases, and every card presented may be used on it. The customer has $10.00 of Finch Notes and presents a Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card with $20.00, a Registry Reward Card with $40.00, a Marlowe & Finch Gift Card with $25.00 and a Merchandise Credit Card with $100.00. Finch Notes pay $10.00, leaving $110.00. The Bonus Card pays $20.00, leaving $90.00. The Registry Reward Card, the only card with an expiry date, pays $40.00, leaving $50.00. Of the remaining cards the lower balance goes first: the Gift Card pays its $25.00, leaving $25.00, and the Merchandise Credit Card pays $25.00, keeping $75.00 on the card.

*Example B — allocation without remainder.* A hypothetical card pays $50.00 across two purchase records due $30.00 and $70.00, together $100.00. The $30.00 record receives thirty hundredths of $50.00, which is $15.00; the $70.00 record receives seventy hundredths of $50.00, which is $35.00. The shares total $50.00 and nothing remains.

*Example C — allocation with a remainder.* A hypothetical card pays $20.00 across three purchase records due $30.00, $30.00 and $45.00, together $105.00. Each $30.00 record's share is $20.00 multiplied by 30 and divided by 105, which is $5.714…, rounded half up to $5.71. The $45.00 record's share is $20.00 multiplied by 45 and divided by 105, which is $8.571…, rounded half up to $8.57. The rounded shares total $19.99, so a remainder of $0.01 is placed on the highest-priced record, the $45.00 record, whose share becomes $8.58.
